thread_analysis.thread_summary: Internal Allion report-review thread (Itsuo Sakai reviewing, Kenichi Ushiroebisu testing/correcting, Kei Tanaka approving) for a Topre Corporation R4H keyboard PTS test report, spanning August 2025. The thread documents a profile-version consistency QA correction (BAS/DIS version numbers) and a follow-up to ensure the corrected reports were actually uploaded before final approval.
all_questions_found: Why must a PTS report's profile version declarations be corrected to match the ICS at test start, and were the revised reports actually uploaded for approval? (see thread_0039_case_01)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread's only technical point (case_01) is a QA review rule: each profile in a PTS report must declare exactly one version number, matching the ICS provided at the start of testing, not an assumed or default value.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Approving a report with an inconsistent or incorrect profile version could produce registration evidence misaligned with the product's actual ICS.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The test engineer initially forgot to upload the revised BAS and DIS reports to the shared approval folder after correcting them, requiring a follow-up reminder before the internal QA reviewer could approve.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Build profile version consistency (matching the ICS at test start) into the standard PTS report review checklist, and confirm corrected reports are actually uploaded to the shared approval location before requesting sign-off.
